$comment: The mechanical half of the port. Everything expressible as 'do this to every file' lives
here; everything that needs judgement lives in `patches/` as a real diff.
The split matters because this runs again on every AndroidX release. A rule survives an
upstream refactor; a patch does not, and a patch that stops applying is a build failure that
names the file a human has to look at. So anything that CAN be a rule is a rule.
$androidOnlyPrefixesComment: Import prefixes with no Kotlin/Wasm implementation. `tools/transform.py` reports every file
still importing one of these after the patches have applied — that report is the worklist.
Deliberately ABSENT, because they already publish wasmJs targets and need no porting at all:
androidx.annotation, androidx.collection, androidx.graphics.shapes (all three have a
*-wasm-js artifact on Google Maven), and every androidx.compose.* package, which is what
Compose Multiplatform republishes. That is why 26 of 222 files need work and not all 222.
$dropAnnotationsComment: Android build-tooling annotations. They carry no runtime meaning, and their absence changes
nothing about what the code does — but their import does not resolve off-Android.
$dropImportsMaterialIconsComment: The last two are not Android-only, they are CMP-missing: `material-icons-core` was deprecated
and then dropped from Compose Multiplatform, so `materialIcon`/`materialPath` have nowhere to
come from. They are re-declared under the SAME NAMES in the same package, by
dropping the import is the entire port: the generated call sites do not change, so
RangeDefaults.kt carries no patch to re-cut when upstream edits it.
$rewriteReferencesComment: One-for-one moves where Compose Multiplatform publishes the same declaration under another
package. `androidx.activity.compose.BackHandler` is the load-bearing one: CMP 1.8 lifted
back handling into `androidx.compose.ui.backhandler`, so the call sites need no edit at all.
$ensureImportsComment: Declarations the Kotlin/JVM compiler default-imports and AndroidX therefore never imports.
In common code they need an import like anything else. The key is a regex looked for in the
file; the value is the import added, in sorted position, when it is missing.

$excludeComment: Files dropped from the generated commonMain because a patch would be the wrong tool — the
Android body is most of the file, and a patch deleting most of a file has to be re-cut
every time any of it moves. Each one is replaced, name for name, by a hand-written file
under `src/commonPort/kotlin` that restates the API the rest of the module compiles
against. Nothing is silently missing: `docs/ANDROID_SURFACE.md` lists every entry.

exclude.androidx/wear/compose/foundation/TouchEx: 138 lines of AccessibilityManager listener plumbing around a one-method interface. Replaced by src/commonPort/.../TouchExplorationStateProvider.kt, which keeps the interface and answers from `platformTouchExplorationEnabled()`.
